Quick summary from initial engineering triage (logs attached):
- Symptom: tenant 3115 saw periodic "stallwaves" where a single hot-key set monopolized the prefetch/batching lanes. This resulted in HOL (head-of-line) blocking on the batch queues and an amplification loop: failed prefetches cause repeated retries which refill the lane, preventing other requests from progressing.
- Metrics: p99 spiked to 3.2s (baseline ~180ms). Error rate ~5% (KV timeouts + 409s from downstream). Overall throughput down ~38% for that tenant’s shards.
- Probable trigger: an aggressive prefetch configuration that was enabled as part of an optimization rollout (small-batch threshold lowered + max-prefetch-window increased) for certain tenants this morning. The change reduced avg latency for normal traffic but created pathological behavior under skewed hotkey distributions.

Immediate mitigation applied at 10:00: - rolled back prefetch window for tenant 3115 to safe defaults, - disabled aggressive prefetch, - quarantined tenant 3115 to a hot-lane isolation group to avoid cross-tenant HOL interference. Initial telemetry shows p99 coming down to ~420ms and error rate falling toward baseline.

Planned next steps:
1) Patch: introduce per-tenant prefetch backpressure and a token-bucket limiter to prevent repeated re-prefetch loops (PR ready, will deploy canary at 13:00 PT).
2) Short-term policy: add a conservative default for small-batch thresholds and enable per-tenant bucketization of KV cache to avoid thrash.
3) Postmortem: capture full traces and write remediation runbook; recommend rolling back the global optimization rollout until we validate against hotkey-skew test harness.

Attachments: prod_config_diff.patch, kv_prefetch_trace_tenant3115.log
